difficulty.obfuscation_note: The bundle is rollup ES output run through javascript-obfuscator with mangled identifier names (seed 8008; no control-flow flattening, string-array or dead-code injection). Inner function-expression names such as the anchor workspaceStateReducer are renamed (the anchor appears as a single-letter declaration in the captured bundle), while renameGlobals:false keeps module-level helper names. Difficulty comes from locating the slot-6 reducer inside a large obfuscated haystack of distractor modules, plus slot-selection structural uncertainty, semantic decoys and async fragmentation.

task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after queueing, routing, snapshot collection, normalization, profile resolution and envelope assembly, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM document click delegation and keydown shortcut, queued and drained asynchronously

evidence: The bundle contains 8 slot configurations in workspaceSlotTable, each with distinct trunk/branch seeds, field formats and base36 widths. Only the slot selected by _k = 3 + 3 = 6 feeds the target field.
The active slot index is encoded as the expression `const _k = 3 + 3`, not a plain literal, making the value non-obvious at first scan.
Core helper names mixToken and spinBits are descriptive but the anchor workspaceStateReducer closure is renamed to a single-letter declaration in the captured bundle.
The exported encodeWorkspaceState calls _workspaceEnc(envelope) where _workspaceEnc is bound at module-init time, decoupling the call site from the slot-selection logic.

The captured bundle embeds 69 inert distractor modules (44 noise + 25 vendor) with thousands of similarly shaped preference helper functions, so the slot-6 reducer must be located within a large obfuscated haystack rather than a small readable file.
The target state code is carried through four async boundaries (microtask, timer, promise and a registry call) before reaching the sink.
The codec registry and the profile resolver both select live functions by string key at runtime, making static analysis insufficient.
Two entry points (pointer click delegation and a keyboard shortcut) feed the same command queue.
The bundle contains 10 decoy state-code-generating functions with similar bit-mixing and hashing algorithms.
role_oracle lists 20 Off-chain entries (11 top-level decoy generators plus 9 helper functions); semantic_decoy_count 7 counts the primary startup and sibling-action decoys.
All 8 workspaceStateReducer closures in workspaceSlotTable share the same function template, so identifying the active one requires tracing _k.
Multiple functions produce 12-character base36 or hex strings near the same save interaction.
Startup initialization executes four decoy state encoders before any user interaction.
The preview, export, sync and reset action handlers execute on the same routed command path as the save handler.
A second codec (encodeContrastState) with a near-identical signature is registered for a sibling profile branch that the exercised trigger does not select.
The command is queued on click/keydown, drained on a microtask plus a zero-delay timer, then routed by string key.
The profile resolver result is awaited through Promise.resolve before the envelope is assembled.
The codec registry resolves the encoder function by a profile-dependent string key, decoupling the anchor from its call site.
The envelope is assembled in a dedicated builder before being handed to the codec.

await routePreferenceCommand(...) inside the drain loop

behavior_category.subtype: save-time workspace preference and appearance state code
behavior_category.reason: The observable value is a stable compact encoding of the user's appearance and workspace preference fields gathered from the settings form. It is not a request signature, browser fingerprint, byte-array transform or request-body rewrite.

near_categories.why_not: The output has no proof/token/seal semantics and is not sent in a network request; it represents stable preference state.
No network request body is emitted or rewritten; the target is a console-observable state code.
The chain encodes local form preference state chosen by the user, not collected browser/device capabilities.

metadata_partitioning_notes.reason: This file describes the task contract, candidate scope and difficulty analysis without exposing the role oracle; only agent_visible/ is distributed to agents.

construct_validity_note.detail: The bundle is lightly obfuscated (mangled locals only) with renameGlobals:false so module-level function names stay readable in captures. The anchor workspaceStateReducer closure is renamed to a single-letter identifier (`b`); difficulty comes from slot-selection structural uncertainty, a 69-module distractor haystack, semantic decoys and async/registry indirection. Keyword search on names such as encode/mix/state can narrow the candidate set quickly; the primary bottleneck is therefore semantic disambiguation among similarly shaped encoders and locating the active slot-6 closure, not call-depth tracing alone.
